To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
women who have unprotected sex with men they distrust and perceive to engage in HIV risky behaviors do so because they have low self esteem and believe that they have little power.
young urban women who engage in unprotected sex with men engaging in HIV risk behaviors are doing so to maintain hope, intimacy, sensuality, stability and strategic gain with a male partner.

women in our sample reported that they engage in unprotected sex with men whom they distrust and perceive to be engaging in HIV risk behaviors in order to maintain hope, intimacy, sensuality, stability, and strategic gain with their male partners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how young urban women’s sex script can be transformed from low to high power sex scripts.
the ways in which women negotiate power and sex in the context of their own lives, their relationships, and the larger social context.
the development of a new paradigm that can provide a basis for a new understanding of the role of power in the lives of urban women and their relationships with men.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the women in this study had a pattern of unprotected sex with men engaging in HIV risk behaviors that is a usual practice that is a low power sex script.

the patterns of unprotected sex with men engaging in HIV risk behaviors can be explained as a usual practice to sustain hope, sensuality and intimacy, strategic gain and stability in a male-female relationship.
the women in this study engaged in unprotected sex as a usual practice to gain power and control in a relationship with a man they trusted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the women in the study had a sense of powerlessness in their sexual relationships.
women who engage in unprotected sex are not just victims of men’s sexual demands.
women’s power is a critical variable for HIV prevention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women’s power to protect themselves from sexual risks is limited by a lack of knowledge of their rights to sexual safety.
women can be powerful and have agency. We need to find ways to help women to see that they can make choices and
women are not powerless victims. They are capable of change and have the potential to make choices to protect themselves from HIV infection
